deep.reconstruction:
The page has three independent research notes, separated by rules. Folio 71 sits between pages of programmatic remarks: the previous page covers quintics, continuation of potentials and the 'critical period'. The next page covers simultaneous rational approximation of (1-z)^a and (1-z)^-a toward the irrationality of 2^sqrt2, and the construction of relatively abelian function fields by division of abelian functions.

(1) TERMINOLOGY OF ALGEBRAIC STRUCTURES. 'Field theory is nothing but a theory of the 4 species (arithmetic operations).' Hilbert classifies number systems by the operations under which they are closed ('invariant'):
- Koerper = closed under +, -, *, / (modern: field).
- Feld = closed under +, -, * (modern: ring).
- Ring = closed under * alone; 'Add' was started and struck out (modern: multiplicative semigroup or monoid).
- Gitter = closed under + and - (modern: additive group or Z-module, a 'lattice' in Minkowski's sense).
This is a hierarchy by closure properties, not a computation.

(2) CONJECTURE ON 'RATIONAL-PRESERVING' HOMEOMORPHISMS. Let Q01 = Q ∩ [0,1].
- Claim A: if phi: Q01 -> Q01 is a bijection, continuous, with phi(1/2) = 1/2 and a derivative, then phi = id. The parenthetical gloss on 'stetig' says intervals go to intervals and larger numbers to larger ones, i.e. phi is order-preserving. An interlinear addition demands a derivative.
- Claim B, the general reformulation: if f is a bijective, continuous, differentiable real function that maps the rationals onto exactly the rationals, then f(x) = (ax+b)/(cx+d) with a, b, c, d rational.
- Link between them (my filling): an increasing bijection of [0,1] fixes 0 and 1. A Moebius map fixing 0, 1/2 and 1 is the identity. So Claim B, restricted to the interval and normalised, yields Claim A.
- Moebius maps with rational coefficients do map P^1(Q) onto itself. On all of R, continuity forces c = 0, i.e. affine maps.

(3) A FUNCTION-FIELD ANALOGUE OF FINITENESS OF THE CLASS NUMBER, FOR A SURFACE. Let K be the field of algebraic functions of two variables, the function field of a surface f = 0 in P^3. 'Finiteness of the number of ideal classes' for K would mean two things:
- (i) there is one algebraic family (Schaar) of point systems (0-cycles);
- (ii) there is one family of curves on f = 0;
- such that every point system and every curve on f = 0 is equivalent to a member of the corresponding family.

Proposed lemma toward this. Given a curve C of order N on f = 0, with N > G(f) for a bound G depending only on the surface, find a curve C' of order < N such that C + C' = (f = 0) ∩ (g = 0) for some surface g of degree m. That is, C + C' ~ mH, where H is the plane section.

Intended induction (my filling): C ~ mH - C' with deg C' < N. Iterating reduces every curve, modulo multiples of H, to plus or minus a curve of order <= G. Curves of bounded order form finitely many algebraic families. Hence divisor classes fall into finitely many families: finite generation of divisors modulo algebraic equivalence plus a continuous part. No proof of the lemma is given; the page ends with the statement.
errors: Claim B (and hence the hope behind Claim A) is false. There exist strictly increasing real-analytic, even entire, bijections of R that map Q onto Q and are not Moebius maps. This was shown by P. Franklin, Trans. AMS 27 (1925), building on Staeckel's 1895 constructions of entire functions with prescribed arithmetic behaviour on countable dense sets. Restricting and normalising such maps gives smooth increasing self-bijections of Q∩[0,1] fixing 1/2 that are not the identity. Hilbert's differentiability hypothesis does not rescue the rigidity.
Claim A as worded needs the order-preserving reading of the parenthesis. Otherwise x -> 1-x is a continuous, differentiable bijection of Q∩[0,1] fixing 1/2 that is not the identity.

Claim B on all of Q: a Moebius map with c != 0 has a pole at -d/c, so it is not a continuous bijection Q -> Q. On R the formula reduces to ax+b; the Moebius form only makes sense on an interval or on P^1.

The order-reduction lemma in (3) is stated without proof and fails without further hypotheses. On a smooth quadric (n=2), a curve of type (a,0) (a lines of one ruling, order a) needs m >= a. The residual of type (m-a, m) then has order 2m - a >= a = N, for every N, so no bound G works for reducible curves. It is at best plausible for irreducible curves and needs an argument (e.g. Riemann-Roch on the surface, which is borderline since sections appear only near m ~ 2N/n).

Statement (i) about point systems: if 'equivalence' is read as rational equivalence of 0-cycles, a single finite-dimensional family representing all classes does not exist in general. Mumford (1968/69) showed CH_0 is infinite-dimensional for surfaces with p_g > 0. The curve statement (ii) is correct in the sense of the Severi/Neron theorem of the base.

results.what: Classification of number systems by closure under the four operations: Koerper (+,-,*,/), Feld (+,-,*), Ring (* only), Gitter (+,-).
results.modern_name: field / ring / multiplicative monoid / additive group (Z-module, lattice)
results.usually_credited_to: Dedekind (Koerper, Ordnung, Modul), Kronecker (Rationalitaetsbereich), Minkowski (Zahlengitter), Hilbert (Zahlring, Zahlbericht 1897)

results.what: Conjecture that every continuous, differentiable bijection mapping exactly the rationals onto the rationals is a rational Moebius map; equivalently, the only increasing differentiable self-bijection of Q∩[0,1] fixing 1/2 is the identity.
results.modern_name: Rigidity question for analytic/smooth maps of countable dense sets (answered negatively by Franklin-type theorems; cf. Barth-Schneider)
results.usually_credited_to: Staeckel 1895 (related constructions); P. Franklin 1925 (counterexample); Barth-Schneider 1970 (general entire-function version)

results.what: Interpretation of finiteness of the ideal-class number for function fields of surfaces: all curves (and point systems) equivalent to members of one algebraic family.
results.modern_name: Theorem of the base (finite generation of Neron-Severi group) plus the Picard variety; for 0-cycles, finite-dimensionality of CH_0 (Bloch/Mumford)
results.usually_credited_to: Severi 1906 (teorema della base), Picard (rho), Neron 1952; Severi 1932 and Mumford 1968 for 0-cycles

results.what: Proposed lemma: every curve of order N > G(f) on f=0 has a residual curve of smaller order in a complete intersection with another surface (order reduction via linkage).
results.modern_name: Linkage / liaison on a surface, residual curves; reduction to bounded degree giving finitely many families (Chow/Hilbert-scheme finiteness)
results.usually_credited_to: Max Noether (Restsatz, residuation), Severi; modern liaison theory (Peskine-Szpiro 1974)

deep.surprise_reason: The page holds two non-routine research ideas, probably from the 1890s. The first is a rigidity conjecture for rational-preserving smooth bijections, later refuted (Franklin 1925). The second is a function-field analogue of class-number finiteness for algebraic surfaces, with a liaison-style order-reduction strategy, which anticipates in programmatic form the Severi base theorem (1906) and the 0-cycle question later settled by Mumford. The pre-Zahlbericht terminology (Feld/Ring/Gitter) is a notable detail. Nothing is proved here, and one conjecture is false, so this is interesting unpublished context rather than a major priority claim.

checkable.sympy: a,b,c,d=symbols('a b c d'); f=lambda x:(a*x+b)/(c*x+d); solve([f(0), f(Rational(1,2))-Rational(1,2), f(1)-1],[a,b,c],dict=True)
checkable.asserts: A Moebius map fixing 0, 1/2 and 1 has b=0, c=0, a=d, i.e. it is the identity, so Claim B (normalised) implies Claim A.
x->1-x fixes 1/2 and is a differentiable bijection of Q∩[0,1], so Claim A needs the order-preserving hypothesis.
x^3+x is a strictly increasing polynomial map Q->Q that is not onto Q (1 is not attained by a rational), illustrating that 'onto Q' is a strong condition.

On a quadric, the residual of a type-(a,0) curve in an (m,m) complete intersection (m>=a) has order 2m-a >= a, so the residual is never of smaller order: counterexample to the reduction lemma for reducible curves (expression equals 0, i.e. 2m-a-a = 2(m-a) >= 0).

checkable.sympy: a,b,c,d,x=symbols('a b c d x'); g=(a*x+b)/(c*x+d); simplify(diff(g,x)-(a*d-b*c)/(c*x+d)**2)==0
checkable.asserts: The Moebius derivative is (ad-bc)/(cx+d)^2, so the map is monotone on intervals avoiding the pole, consistent with the bijectivity requirement when ad-bc != 0.

It seems to say approximately '(d.h. so dass zweien Grössen alle innerhalb derselben wieder 2 grössere entsprechen)', i.e. intervals map to intervals and order is preserved. The machine reading 'so dass zwei immer alle innerhalb [?] wieder 2 grössere entsprechen' is garbled.

'Punkt{+systeme+}[-gruppen-]': 'systeme' is written above the struck-out 'gruppen'; the reading is correct.
